findings.title: Light-theme lightness value changed unintentionally (30% -> 70%) while adding dark variant
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. The PR's goal is only to add a dark-theme counterpart via `dark-light-choose()`, but the light-theme value itself was changed to 70% instead of being preserved as 30%: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`. This is inconsistent with every other conversion in the PR (which keeps the original percentage as the first argument and mirrors it as `100-X` for the second argument), and it silently alters the light-theme appearance of this text (now much lighter/lower-contrast than before), which is an unintended visual regression unrelated to the stated purpose of the PR.

findings.title: Arguments to dark-light-choose swapped/incorrect for .custom-message-length
findings.body: Original rule: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);`. Expected conversion (per the pattern used everywhere else in this PR) would be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, preserving the light-theme value and mirroring for dark. Instead the diff produces `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` — the two percentages are swapped relative to the expected mapping. This both changes the light-theme color unintentionally (from 70% to 30% lightness) and produces an incorrect (also swapped) value for the dark theme.

findings.title: group-member-info .name lightness value changed unintentionally (30% -> 50%)
findings.body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` (note: the sibling `.title` rule a few lines below correctly preserves its 50% value). In this conversion, the value was changed to 50%/50% instead of preserving 30% and mirroring to 70% as done consistently elsewhere in the PR: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. This silently changes the light-theme text color for group member names, an unintended regression.

findings.title: group-member-info .name lightness value changed unintentionally (30% -> 50%), same bug as desktop/user.scss
findings.body: Same issue as in desktop/user.scss: the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` but the conversion produced `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`, changing the light-theme value from 30% to 50% instead of preserving it and mirroring to 70% for the dark variant. This is an unintended visual regression for the light theme on mobile user pages.

findings.title: topic-map h3 lightness value changed unintentionally (20% -> 50%)
findings.body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);`. The equivalent desktop rule (desktop/topic-post.scss h3 inside .topic-map) was correctly converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`, preserving 20%. However the mobile version here was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`, changing the light-theme lightness from 20% to 50%. This creates an unintended, inconsistent visual regression between desktop and mobile for the same heading style.
